title: Update SDK example snippets to match Quickstart template conventions (client init, retries, OTel context)
creator: Monica Patel
description:
Goal
Refactor Redwood SDK example snippets (Python + TypeScript) to match the new Quickstart Template patterns so users don’t see conflicting guidance between docs/SDK READMEs and template-generated apps.

Background / Why
We’re shipping production-minded Quickstart templates (RAG + agents) with standardized safe defaults and observability conventions. Today, the SDK repos and docs contain snippets that:
- initialize clients differently than templates (different env var names, different default timeouts)
- omit retry/backoff guidance (or recommend naïve retry for streaming)
- don’t show span context propagation or request-id capture
This creates onboarding confusion and makes it harder for Support/Solutions Eng to debug issues because traces/logs don’t match our recommended taxonomy.

Scope
In scope:
- Update public-facing snippets in:
  - redwood-sdk-python README / docs pages where we show basic chat/completions + streaming
  - redwood-sdk-typescript README / docs pages for chat + streaming
  - redwood-docs SDK guide snippets that are effectively “copy/paste first request”
- Make snippets match template conventions:
  - client initialization via env-based config (no hardcoded secrets)
  - explicit timeout + retry policy calls/parameters matching safe defaults
  - span context propagation hooks and request id propagation into logs (where available)
  - consistent header/tag usage for correlation, but keep template adoption telemetry opt-in
- Add a short “production defaults” note linking to templates for full scaffolding (don’t turn SDK READMEs into a template walkthrough).

Out of scope:
- Adding new SDK features (tracked elsewhere; we will consume whatever is merged in ENG-4189/SDK PRs)
- Changing gateway behavior or header allowlists (tracked in platform work)
- Building new examples/apps; this ticket is snippets + docs alignment.

Template conventions to mirror
- Env vars: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_BASE_URL (when applicable), REDWOOD_MODEL (or MODEL)
- Timeouts/retries: follow template safe defaults (timeouts on connect + per-request; bounded retries with exponential backoff + jitter; do not blindly retry streaming bodies)
- Observability: OTel spans around “llm.request”, “llm.stream”, “tool.call” (when present), and consistent attributes; log redaction guidance; request id capture (x-redwood-request-id)
- Error taxonomy: auth/quota/network/tool/retrieval errors should be recognizable and include a stable error code/shape where SDK supports it.

Acceptance criteria
- Python snippets:
  - Basic non-streaming request snippet aligns with template client init + timeout/retry guidance.
  - Streaming snippet demonstrates safe handling: cancellation, partial outputs, and non-destructive retry strategy (retry only on initial connect / before first token).
  - Example shows capturing request id from response headers (or SDK helper) and attaching it to logs.
  - OTel example shows how to wrap the client call inside a span (or use SDK helper if present) and how to propagate context (web framework note acceptable).
- TypeScript snippets:
  - Same alignment as Python: init, streaming robustness note, request-id capture, OTel-friendly hooks.
- Docs alignment:
  - Redwood docs SDK snippets that overlap with templates updated to match the above.
  - All snippets reference the same env var names and do not hardcode secrets.
- Verification:
  - Snippet code paths were executed at least once locally (simple smoke run) and linted/typed.
  - Links from docs to templates and templates back to SDK docs are consistent.

Implementation plan
1) Inventory existing snippets
- Identify all copy/paste blocks in:
  - redwood-sdk-python (README + docs pages)
  - redwood-sdk-typescript (README + docs pages)
  - redwood-docs pages that show SDK usage
- Categorize by type: basic request, streaming request, retries/timeouts, instrumentation.

2) Define canonical snippet patterns (single source of truth)
- Use the template code as canonical (Quickstart repo) and backport the minimal necessary parts into SDK examples.
- Keep snippets short; include “See template for full production scaffolding” link.

3) Update snippets + open PRs
- Python:
  - Update client init and timeout defaults to mirror template safe defaults (and SDK standardization PRs).
  - Add request-id extraction example.
  - Add an OTel example using the new tracing helpers if available.
- TypeScript:
  - Update streaming snippet to match reconnect/error typing from TS SDK work.
  - Add OTel-friendly hooks example if available.
- Docs:
  - Update docs blocks that reference old init patterns.

4) Review
- DevEx review (Monica Patel)
- Observability sanity check (Allison Grant or Caleb Johnson): span names/attributes and cardinality concerns
- Support review (Priya Shah): troubleshootability and request-id visibility

5) Rollout
- Merge SDK + docs PRs, then verify templates and docs match in public preview.

Notes / Trade-offs
- We will keep telemetry tagging (template-origin traffic) out of SDK README snippets to avoid privacy/proxy issues. If referenced, it must be explicitly opt-in and documented as optional.
- For streaming retries: we’ll explicitly document that retrying mid-stream can duplicate tokens and should be application-specific. Snippets will only show safe retries before the first token / on connect failures.
- OTel: we’ll keep instrumentation examples minimal (start span, add attributes, propagate context), and point to templates/SDK instrumentation guide for full setup.

Links
- Confluence: SDK instrumentation for quickstarts: sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/sdk-guides/sdk-instrumentation-for-quickstarts.json
- Confluence: Safe defaults and guardrails: sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/safe-defaults-and-guardrails.json
- Observability conventions: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/quickstart-tracing-conventions.json

Related work / PRs
- redwood-sdk-python:
  - PR #612 add tracing context propagation helpers
  - PR #613 standardize timeouts and retry policy
- redwood-sdk-typescript:
  - PR #488 streaming reconnect and better error types
  - PR #489 OTel-friendly hooks
- redwood-docs:
  - PR #841 quickstart templates section + navigation
  - PR #842 RAG agent template walkthrough
  - PR #844 observability hooks reference

Progress updates
2025-02-12 (Sabrina)
- Did snippet inventory across Python + TS READMEs and flagged 7 blocks that diverge from template patterns (env var names, retries, streaming handling).
- Pulled template defaults from safe-defaults doc; drafted canonical snippet shape for both languages.

2025-02-20 (Sabrina)
- Opened draft PRs for SDK repos updating init + retry/timeouts and adding request-id logging examples.
- Waiting on ENG-4189 request-id propagation helpers landing so snippets don’t rely on private response objects.

2025-03-03 (Allison)
- Reviewed OTel snippet attributes; requested we avoid adding user_id/session_id attributes by default to prevent high-cardinality metrics. OK to include redwood.request_id and model name.

2025-03-10 (Monica)
- Approved final snippet language. Confirmed we’re not including template telemetry headers in SDK snippets (opt-in only).

Done criteria / Closure
- SDK snippets match template conventions and were smoke-tested.
- Docs snippets updated where overlap exists.
- Support can ask customers to “copy/paste the SDK snippet” and see request ids + basic spans consistent with templates.

Post-launch follow-ups (not blocking)
- Add a short ‘doctor’ checklist link in SDK docs (“If you used the template CLI, run: redwood doctor”).
- Consider moving code blocks to a snippet-testing harness in CI to prevent drift (propose new ENG ticket if we see regressions).
